records.summary: 3034 24th St lies in the NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning district where a Restaurant is a conditional use. The property sits inside both the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (which requires Conditional Use for any proposed restaurant in this sub-area) and the Calle 24 Special Use District (which prohibits new restaurants where they would exceed 35% of commercial frontage within 300 ft, though the records do not show the current share). The site has one prior planning record: a 2009 referral for a restaurant use that was denied because building violations from fire damage had not been abated. The immediate block is saturated with food and drink businesses: 14 registered establishments within 500 ft (N=14), 3 bars, and 6 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, triggering an undue-concentration flag. Within 1,000 ft in this zoning district over the last 10 years there were only 5 dated use decisions for comparable businesses (1 approved, 2 approved with conditions, 0 denied, 2 withdrawn)—too few for a rate.

patterns.pattern: Restaurants converting from retail or other non-food uses in NCT-24TH-MISSION require Conditional Use Authorization and Planning Commission hearings; continuation-of-use referrals are approved quickly but do not apply to change-of-use situations.

Restaurant CUAs in NCT-24TH-MISSION within the Mission Alcohol SUD have been consistently approved over 30+ years (1990, 1994, 2001, 2011, 2019, 2025) when the concept is food-focused and not proposing bar use, even in a high-density restaurant corridor.

Approved restaurant CUAs on the 24th Street corridor routinely carry standard conditions for eating and drinking uses: hours of operation (often to 2 AM even without late-night entertainment), odor control equipment on plans, soundproofing, sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, garbage kept inside, and appointment of a community liaison.

The subject property (3034 24th St) has a 2009 denial on record for a restaurant referral, but the denial was purely due to unabated building violations from fire damage, not opposition to the restaurant use itself; verification of abatement is essential before filing.

Not all restaurant CUA applications proceed to approval; at least one nearby case (2801 Folsom, office-to-banquet room) was withdrawn within three weeks of filing in 2018, though the record does not state the reason.

The 24th Street corridor between Folsom and Mission has seen restaurant approvals on parcels ranging from small (25 ft × 100 ft) to large (50 ft wide), and for concepts ranging from small self-service cafes to full-service restaurants, showing flexibility in the types of food uses the Commission will approve.

findings.text: In NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning a first-story restaurant is a conditional use under Planning Code § 763, in force from January 14, 2024.

The property lies inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires Conditional Use Authorization for any proposed restaurant in the sub-area east of Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street (Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1)).

The Calle 24 Special Use District prohibits a new restaurant where restaurants, limited restaurants and bars take up more than 35% of the commercial frontage (in linear feet) within 300 ft of the site inside the district (Planning Code § 249.59(d)(1)). The records do not show the current percentage.

A 2009 Planning referral for a restaurant use at 3034 24th Street (MB0901179) was denied because building violations from fire damage were not abated; the Planning Commission stated the proposed use could open only when DBI cleared all violations.
The immediate area has 14 food or drink businesses within 500 ft (N=14), including 3 bars, and 6 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, raising an undue-concentration flag.

In NCT-24TH-MISSION within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, 3 of N=5 dated restaurant CUA decisions were approved (1 approved, 2 approved with conditions), 0 denied, and 2 withdrawn; too few cases for a rate. A February 2025 CUA at 2937 24th St (166 m away) for a restaurant change of use was approved 6–0 with standard conditions.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate a food facility is required and is issued by DPH after plan check, inspection and confirmation of a certified food safety manager on staff; no hearing is required.

findings.text: Every food or drink business needs a health permit to operate, issued by SF Department of Public Health after plan check and final inspection confirm the facility matches approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff (California Retail Food Code §§ 114380–114381; SF Health Code Article 8).
The DPH permit application is referred to SF Planning for a zoning review; this referral step is part of the health permit process, not a separate approval.

approvals.summary: A building permit with change of use is required for the tenant improvements and the retail-to-restaurant conversion; the permit must conform to the Planning Code and will be referred to Planning for zoning review.

findings.text: A change of use from retail to restaurant is a change of use under Planning Code § 102.

The proposed occupancy group under the Building Code is not established because the description does not state whether the space is for fewer than 50 people; a restaurant or bar is Assembly Group A-2, and a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B (2022 California Building Code §§ 303.1.1, 303.3).
The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records; only plans or an inspection show it.

A building permit application with a change of use is referred to the Planning Department for zoning review (Planning Code § 175(a)); this referral step is part of the building permit process, not a separate approval.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation limited to 6:00 AM to 2:00 AM Monday through Sunday.
expected_conditions.basis: A November 2019 CUA at 2956 24th Street (118 m away, NCT-24TH-MISSION) conditioned the restaurant to operate 6 AM–2 AM (Motion under Case No. 2018-013158CUA). This is the standard hours limit for eating and drinking uses in this district.

expected_conditions.condition: Install and maintain odor control equipment in conformance with approved plans to prevent noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises; odor control ducting shall not be applied to the primary façade.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2018-013158CUA approval at 2956 24th Street required odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the building permit plans. This condition appears in the standard eating-and-drinking-use conditions for the district.

expected_conditions.condition: The premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels in the SF Noise Control Ordinance.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2018-013158CUA approval required soundproofing as part of the standard eating and drinking use conditions. Soundproofing is a recurring condition for restaurant CUAs in mixed-use buildings in this district.

expected_conditions.condition: Maintain the main entrance and all abutting sidewalks in a clean and sanitary condition per DPW Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards, and monitor the sidewalk within a one-block radius daily during business hours to keep it free of litter associated with the business.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2018-013158CUA approval required daily sidewalk monitoring within a one-block radius and maintenance per SF Police Code Article 1, § 34. This is a standard condition for eating and drinking uses.

expected_conditions.condition: Keep garbage, recycling and compost containers within the premises and hidden from public view, and place them outside only when being serviced; trash shall be contained and disposed of per DPW guidelines.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2018-013158CUA approval required garbage containers to be kept inside and hidden from public view. This is a standard condition for eating and drinking uses in the district.

expected_conditions.condition: Prior to issuance of a building permit, appoint a community liaison officer to deal with issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties, and provide the Zoning Administrator and registered neighborhood groups with the liaison's name, business address and telephone number.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2018-013158CUA approval required appointment of a community liaison prior to building permit issuance. This is a standard condition for new restaurant CUAs in the district.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain written confirmation from SF Department of Building Inspection that the 2009 building violations from fire damage at 3034 24th Street have been abated.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a property records search for parcel 3640/071 and a written statement of the current violation status. Reference the November 2009 Planning referral MB0901179, which stated that the restaurant use could open only when DBI cleared all violations from fire damage. If violations remain open, obtain a scope of work to abate them and add that work to the tenant improvement budget and timeline. Do not file any application or sign a lease until DBI confirms the property is clear.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with SF Planning to confirm compliance with Calle 24 SUD § 249.59(d)(1) and the zoning pathway.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a zoning determination or pre-application review for a 1,540-square-foot restaurant at 3034 24th Street in NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning, inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD and the Calle 24 SUD. Ask Planning to calculate the current percentage of commercial frontage within 300 feet devoted to restaurants, limited restaurants and bars to confirm whether the project is below the 35% cap under § 249.59(d)(1). Confirm the CUA pathway, application requirements and fee estimate. Bring a preliminary floor plan and a description of the concept (limited cooking, no alcohol, closes before midnight, not a chain).

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning (Case Type: Conditional Use) for a restaurant use at 3034 24th Street.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application with a project narrative explaining that the concept is a neighborhood-serving restaurant with limited cooking, no alcohol service, and hours closing before midnight. Emphasize that the use is food-focused (not a bar) and is consistent with the pattern of restaurant approvals on the 24th Street corridor over the last 30 years. Include a floor plan, elevations if the façade changes, a menu or concept description, and photographs of the existing conditions. State that the business is independently owned (not formula retail) if that is the case. Request any fee waiver (e.g. First Year Free) if the operator qualifies. The application fee is approximately $3,100 for a CUA with no construction, adjusted annually for CPI.

filing_playbook.action: Conduct the required pre-application community meeting and post the 30-day notice at the property and mail it to owners and occupants within 300 feet.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: SF Planning will schedule or instruct you to hold a community meeting before the hearing. Invite neighbors, the neighborhood association and nearby businesses. Present the concept, emphasize the food focus, the lack of alcohol and late-night hours, and the commitment to good-neighbor practices (sidewalk maintenance, garbage management, odor control, soundproofing). Solicit feedback and address concerns. Post the yellow notice at the property for 30 days and mail it to all owners and occupants within 300 feet per Planning Code § 311. Bring proof of mailing and posting to the hearing.

filing_playbook.action: Appear at the Planning Commission hearing and present the project.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At the hearing (typically 6–10 months after filing), present the concept as a neighborhood-serving restaurant that fits the corridor's 30-year pattern of food-service approvals. Reference comparable approvals (2015-002658CUA-02 approved February 2025 at 2937 24th St, 2018-013158CUA approved 2019 at 2956 24th St, and 2011.0496C approved 2011 at 2962 24th St). Commit to the expected conditions: hours to 2 AM or earlier, odor control equipment, soundproofing, sidewalk maintenance within one block, garbage kept inside, and a community liaison. If the Commission requests modifications, agree to reasonable conditions and ask for approval subject to those conditions.

filing_playbook.action: File a building permit application with SF Department of Building Inspection for tenant improvements and change of use, after Planning Commission approval.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the building permit application with architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect, showing the kitchen layout, equipment, finishes, plumbing, electrical and mechanical systems. Include the occupant load calculation and the occupancy group classification. Request routing to DPH for plan check, Fire for hood suppression review if applicable, and Planning for zoning conformance review per § 175. The building permit is referred to Planning, which will confirm that the work conforms to the approved CUA. Coordinate plan check comments with your architect and respond promptly to expedite approval.

filing_playbook.action: Submit a Public Health plan check application concurrently with or immediately after the building permit application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File the DPH plan check application online through the Environmental Health portal with two sets of scaled drawings, interior and exterior photos, a menu, and the business registration number. The fee is $828 for a small remodel or $2,207 for a new restaurant (FY 2026–27). DPH will review the kitchen layout, equipment, finishes, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, and compliance with the California Retail Food Code. Schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% completion and a final inspection before opening. Book inspections at least two weeks in advance with your plan reviewer.

filing_playbook.action: After the final DPH and DBI inspections pass, apply for the Health Permit to Operate online.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the Permit to Operate application with your business registration number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), federal EIN, and proof that at least one certified food safety manager is on staff. The application fee is $470 (FY 2026–27); the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28. DPH will issue the permit after confirming the facility matches the approved plans and the manager certification is on file. The permit must be posted at the premises before opening to the public.

timeline_cost.notes: These figures are the time to approval and government cost for the Conditional Use Authorization, Health permit to operate, and Building permit with change of use, drawn from the catalog and comparable cases. Time: 165–435 days is the range from filing to approval. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days from filing to Commission approval (catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization), with one comparable decided in 408 days (2018-013158CUA, filed Sept 2018, decided Nov 2019) and another in 20 days (2015-002658CUA-02, filed Dec 2024, decided Feb 2025, though that was an extension of a prior authorization). Add 14–120 days for the building permit and 14–45 days for the health permit, which can run in parallel after CUA approval. Cost: $5,600–$19,300 covers CUA application ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction valuation and fee waiver eligibility), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500), DPH Permit to Operate ($470), and building permit fees ($800–$15,000 as a percentage of construction valuation). Not included: business registration ($55–$700), entity formation ($70–$150), architect and consultant fees, construction costs, or the time to resolve the 2009 building violations if they remain open. The Calle 24 SUD frontage calculation may prohibit the project entirely; obtain that determination before filing.
